title: Per-Insured Aggregate Face Limit and Acceleration Aggregation — Term Life Insurance
content:
## Provision

Term Life Insurance coverage is aggregated per insured life, the insured being identified by insured name and date of birth, across every owner and every term policy. A new policy is issued only if the face amount on the insured after issue does not exceed **10000000 US dollars**.

The face amount on the insured after issue is the total face amount, at the evaluation date, of every Ashgrove term policy on the same insured (same insured name and date of birth) whose status is applied, in force or grace period, plus the new face amount. Policies that are lapsed, converted, expired, cancelled or closed by claim do not count.

Terminal illness accelerations are also aggregated per insured. The amount accelerated on one insured is the total of every terminal illness advance paid, over the lifetime of every Ashgrove term policy on the same insured, whatever its owner or status; it may never exceed the product's maximum acceleration amount of the policy being accelerated.

## Worked boundary (hypothetical figures)

| Face already counted on the insured | New face | Face on the insured after issue | Issued? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 9500000 | 500000 | 10000000 | yes — equal to the limit does not exceed it |
| 9500000 | 500001 | 10000001 | no |
| 9500000 (plus a lapsed policy of 2000000) | 500000 | 10000000 | yes — the lapsed policy does not count |

## Points of judgement

- Policies owned by different owners on the same insured are counted together.
- A policy in its grace period still counts toward the face on the insured; a converted one does not.
- For accelerations, advances already paid on any term policy on the insured count, including policies no longer in force.
